spatial_claims.claim: BC is a line segment divided at point D, with BD the greater part and DC the lesser
EF is a breadth produced by applying the square on A to BC (area application: BC x EF = A^2)
L is a line segment equal to BD - DC
BC x L = BD^2 - DC^2 by algebraic identity 2.5

configuration_map: Point D on segment BC divides it into BD (greater term) and DC (lesser term). EF is a length defined by area application (BC x EF = A^2). L is a length equal to BD - DC. All other reasoning concerns commensurability ratios, rational areas, and proportions among these magnitudes. No complex geometric configuration is constructed — no points inside/outside figures, no angle decompositions, no ray orderings, no circle positions.
skip_reason: The proof is purely algebraic/proportional, dealing entirely with Book 10 commensurability theory (rational lines, binomials, apotomes, commensurability in square, numerical ratios, and area commensurability). The only spatial elements are trivial 1D point-on-segment configurations and standard area applications. There are no geometric configuration claims (no interior/exterior points, no angle decompositions, no ray orderings, no circle positions) that could be checked for spatial consistency contradictions.
